Subject: Routing exception + UK Addendum request for legacy analytics subprocessor

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the demo last week. A quick ask as procurement pulls the DPA together: OpenHealth operates an older analytics vendor (AnalyticaLegacy Inc.) that currently processes de-identified event logs in the US. We cannot migrate that vendor to EU processing within the next 6 months due to contractual binding with our care analytics contract.

Can Redwood accept a scoped routing exception (limited to one subprocessor, limited data types) with compensating controls, and then include that scope in the UK Addendum / TIA appendices? Our legal prefers a specific carve-out rather than a blanket transfer clause. I attached a vendor matrix for reference.

Key asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a per-customer carve-out in the UK Addendum / TIA?
- If not, what evidence or mitigations do you need to evaluate it?
- Timeline: procurement needs a view by EOD next Tues (9/19) to keep our quarter close.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Ellen Marc
Senior Legal Ops | OpenHealth Systems

Priya / team —

Quick technical note from Security/Compliance perspective: we can accept a narrowly-scoped carve-out but require the following minimum compensating controls: 

1) Field-level pseudonymization: personal identifiers (name, national id, full DOB) must be removed before any transfer; hashed IDs with per-customer salt are acceptable.
2) Access restrictions: the legacy subprocessor must only receive hashed records; no joins permitted. RBAC enforced; admin access audited.
3) Data minimization & retention: max 90 days retention for raw event logs; aggregated outputs can be kept per contract.
4) Enhanced logging & SIEM integration: all access and API calls to the legacy subprocessor must be forwarded to Redwood logging; retention 180 days for audit.
5) Audit rights: OpenHealth or an approved auditor gets quarterly sampling rights, 30-day turnaround on evidence requests.

If those are acceptable, Legal can accept a clause in the UK Addendum that points to a customer-specific TIA appendix stating the carve-out and the controls. I attached a short safeguards matrix to illustrate what we'll commit to and what requires a technical change.

Caveat: if the subprocessor performs re-identification/joining operations in the US, we cannot accept the carve-out.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Director, Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_tia-safeguards_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

Ellen / Tom —

Summary and proposed next steps (per internal review):

Decision: Redwood will accept a narrowly-scoped per-customer carve-out for AnalyticaLegacy Inc., limited to hashed event logs and metadata only, provided the following compensating controls are contractually bound in a customer-specific TIA appendix and referenced in the UK Addendum / DPA amendment:

- Exact scope: only event-level records (event_type, event_ts, hashed_event_id, metadata fields listed in Exhibit A). No PII joins or identifiers.
- Controls bundle (commitments): field-level pseudonymization (per-customer salt), RBAC + restricted API tokens, 90-day raw retention, aggregated outputs allowed per contract, forwarding of access logs to Redwood SIEM (180-day retention), quarterly sampling audits with 30-day evidence turnaround, and a documented escalation path if subprocessor declines audit (Redwood will provide attestation and/or airlocked exports).
- Legal: Redwood will produce DPA amendment redlines and a UK Addendum paragraph referencing the TIA appendix. Draft redlines attached; target DocuSign issuance by 9/26.

Action items / owners:
- Priya: finalize DPA amendment redlines and TIA appendix draft (attached) — due 9/22 EOD.
- Kimberly / Marcus: confirm implementation timeline for logging + per-customer salt within dev ops — due 9/24.
- OpenHealth procurement: confirm acceptance of controls bundle and sign-off by 9/26 to meet SOW schedule.

If OpenHealth wants a stronger bridge, we can add an optional 6-month revisit clause to move processing onshore if your vendor contract permits.

I will post the final DPA amendment to the Drive and route the DocuSign link once legal confirms.
